Article Title: Phones confiscated, players sent home: Match-fixing cloud hangs over Pakistan cricket again
Article Text:
Pakistan's Babar Azam celebrates after taking a catch to dismiss England's Ben Duckett during the second Test at the Lord's against England. (AP)

Every match of a series is important for us and we are not left with any option if a player is not performing but to look for his replacement. The purpose behind these changes is not to axe players from contention, but just to replace them Mohsin Naqvi | PCB Chairman

(The story will be updated once we receive responses to our queries.)

NEW DELHI: The ghost of match-fixing has returned to haunt the Pakistan cricket team and the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) during the ongoing three-match Test series against England. After losing the second Test by 194 runs at Lord's, PCB decided to drop Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha, Imam-ul-Haq, Ali Usman, Khurram Shahzad, Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Zafar. Sarfaraz Ahmed, the head coach, and Umar Gul, the bowling coach, were also released from their duties.In their place, seven players have been drafted into the squad, including five yet to make their international debuts. The two capped players are batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, while the uncapped group comprises pace-bowling all-rounders Razaullah Khan and Mohammad Imran, left-arm spinner Arafat Minhas, wicketkeeper Saad Baig and left-arm pacer Mohammad Imran Junior.It has been learnt that the drastic changes being made within Pakistan cricket were driven by reasons that were “more than cricket” and not merely a fallout of the team's dismal performances. We have reached out to the concerned parties for a comment, including hosts the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) and PCB. More than 72 hours later, we received no response.However, Amir Mir, PCB's Director Media and Digital Communications, issued a public statement: "The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally.The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration. "According to Pakistani outlet 365 News, the players' devices have been handed over to the PCB and will remain in the board's custody until the conclusion of the final Test. The report did not disclose the identities of the players whose phones were confiscated, while the PCB has not publicly explained why the devices were taken into custody.A couple of days after making sweeping changes to the squad, PCB Director of High Performance Aaqib Javed launched a scathing attack on opening batter Imam-ul-Haq, who suffered a low-grade calf tear at Lord's. Aaqib criticised Imam for not batting in either innings of the Lord's Test and vowed to “take action” against him."The Imam injury is a big question mark, and a deep disappointment. Players in the past used to get injuries, but they used to put on casts and still tried to play. We'll take action against this. How is it possible that a pulled muscle ruled you out of batting in both innings? He should have tried and fought. He'll have to face an inquiry; I can't say he faked it, but a muscle pull like that cannot stop you from batting altogether," Aaqib said in an interview with Pakistan broadcast network Geo.Aqib had also defended the number of changes that were made mid-series. "The message we're sending to the recalled players is that you have to raise your game on important tours and compete, and we should be able to see some effort," he said.PCB Chairman Mohsin Naqvi echoed Aaqib Javed's sentiments and defended their knee-jerk reaction in a vociferous manner. "Every match of a series is important for us and we are not left with any option if a player is not performing but to look for his replacement. The purpose behind these changes is not to axe players from contention, but just to replace them," Naqvi told Geo Network.Incidentally, Lord's was the venue for one of the biggest spot-fixing scandal in cricket and it involved the Pakistan cricket team. Then, captain Salman Butt, Mohammad Asif and Mohammad Amir were handed prison sentences and banned for taking bribes from a bookmaker to deliberately bowl no-balls at certain pre-aranged moments during the Test match in 2010.
Article Summary: PCB Chairman Mohsin Naqvi echoed Aaqib Javed's sentiments and defended their knee-jerk reaction. Sarfaraz Ahmed, the head coach, and Umar Gul, the bowling coach, were also released from their duties. Seven players have been drafted into the squad, including five yet to make their international debuts.

Article Title: The America-Russia Paradox: One chases historic gold at Chess Olympiad, the other not allowed to play
Article Text:
America's Levon Aronian and Russia's Ian Nepomniachtchi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: For most of the 20th century, the Chess Olympiad was one of the few arenas where the Cold War actually played out on a board. The Soviet Union treated the biennial team event as a matter of state prestige, fielding lineups stacked with world champions and winning eighteen gold medals between 1952 and 1990.The United States, briefly dominant in the 1930s behind Frank Marshall's golden generation, spent the second half of the century chasing that shadow. They came closest in 1976, when it won gold only because the Soviets and their Eastern Bloc allies boycotted the tournament in Haifa, Israel, over FIDE's refusal to move the venue. Bobby Fischer's defeat of Boris Spassky in Reykjavik in 1972 remains the sport's most mythologised individual clash, but the Olympiad was always the collective version of the same rivalry. Both sides were present.Fifty years on, the framing has flipped entirely. Russia inherited the Soviet Union's chess machine after 1991 and kept winning through the 2000s, eventually matching the United States with six Olympiad golds apiece.But as the 46th Chess Olympiad approaches in Samarkand from September 15–27, it is the United States sending a stacked five-man roster chasing team glory, and Russia, for a third consecutive cycle, are not able to send anyone at all.Levon Aronian will play for Team USA this September, alongside Fabiano Caruana, Wesley So, Hans Niemann and Awonder Liang, with IM John Donaldson captaining and GM Grigory Oparin as trainer.It will be Aronian's third Olympiad since he switched federations from Armenia, a country for which he won gold as part of three separate Olympiad-winning teams, to the United States in late 2021. He debuted for the US in Chennai in 2022, won team silver on board four in Budapest in 2024, and now arrives in Samarkand with an unusually specific ambition."I was thinking that it would be a good time to win an Olympiad because I don't know if there are many people who have won four Olympiads," Aronian told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction. "I haven't checked. I would like to join that club."Asked which teams stood in the way beyond the obvious contenders besides India, Aronian didn't hesitate to name a few."It's going to be tough against Uzbekistan. I also think China can be very strong; they always have underrated players," the veteran Grandmaster opined. "Traditionally, Armenia can play well, and this time, I think Germany is also a good team."Currently playing for Ganges Grandmasters at the Global Chess League (GCL), he feels the league could be a useful rehearsal for exactly the kind of pressure he will be facing at the Chess Olympiad."There's always tension in this tournament. Teams want to play well. It's good to simulate that situation where everything depends on you. It always happens," the 43-year-old Grandmaster added.On the other hand, though, there will be no equivalent build-up for Ian Nepomniachtchi. The current Russian No. 1 and a two-time World Championship challenger will not be in Samarkand, after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ordered FIDE to suspend the Russian Chess Federation following a complaint from Ukraine's federation over tournaments staged in occupied territory.FIDE's Council complied only partially with the ruling, prompting protests from several national federations. The politics reached the top of the sport itself in July, when FIDE president Arkady Dvorkovich, a former Russian deputy prime minister, voluntarily stepped aside from his duties after being added to the European Union's sanctions list."It's very unfortunate," the 36-year-old Russian Grandmaster told this website exclusively on the sidelines of GCL. "What makes it even worse is that we had very high hopes. Russian sport is getting back this year, with a lot of teams in other sports participating in World Championships. We would expect chess to be one of those too."But maybe the fact that Dvorkovich got onto the sanctions list early this summer brought some changes. There was also the unfortunate CAS case, which didn't go well for the Russian Chess Federation. Even after that, we expected Russia to participate, maybe in neutral status," Nepo added. However, the wish to play under a neutral flag has not been granted.Not being too critical of the situation, he just hopes that everything gets sorted out for the sake of the sport. "Belarus is playing, and Russia is not. Hopefully things will get better; for sport, and not just for sport," the Ganges Grandmaster icon player remarked.Set side by side, the two situations barely resemble the same sport.One player is refining a personal record, treating a franchise league as a dress rehearsal for a tournament he expects to win.Also Read: 8 months, Moscow-to-Munich flights, but now he is 'fed up': Behind Russia No. 1 Ian Nepomniachtchi's tattoos The other is watching a competition happen without him, for reasons that have nothing to do with how he plays chess.It's a reminder that the Olympiad, for all its history as a proxy battlefield between Washington and Moscow, was at least always a battlefield both sides got to enter. In Samarkand this year, just like the previous two editions, only one of them will.
Article Summary: The 46th Chess Olympiad will take place in Samarkand from September 15-27. The United States is sending a stacked five-man roster chasing team glory. Russia, for a third consecutive cycle, are not able to send anyone at all. Levon Aronian will play for Team USA, while Ian Nepomniachtchi will represent Russia.

Article Title: ‘Couldn't stay silent’: Iranian footballers reveal why they refused to sing anthem before seeking asylum in Australia
Article Text:
Iran women's football player Fatemeh Pasandideh salutes during the national anthem of Iran. (AP Photo)

‘We just wanted to stand with our people’

Silence becomes a turning point

‘I couldn't stay silent’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

‘I don't want to put their lives in danger’

Iranian footballers Atefeh Ramezanisadeh and Fatemeh Pasandideh have broken their silence over the protest that preceded their decision to seek asylum in Australia, confirming that their refusal to sing Iran's national anthem at the Women's Asian Cup was a deliberate act of defiance against Tehran.The two players, who abandoned the Iranian delegation after the tournament and remained in Australia, spoke publicly for the first time since claiming asylum. Their interview with Australia's 60 Minutes was broadcast on Sunday, shedding new light on a gesture that had sparked intense debate over whether the players were mourning their country amid the escalating conflict or protesting against Iran's government.For Ramezanisadeh, 34, and Pasandideh, 22, the message was clear: they were standing with protesters back home.Iran's women's team had remained silent when the national anthem was played before their opening match against South Korea on March 2. The refusal immediately drew criticism in Iran, with sections of the country's media branding the players as traitors.At the time, however, the team did not publicly explain the decision.The gesture came shortly after US and Israeli attacks on Iran began on February 28, leading some observers to interpret the silence as an act of mourning. Others saw it as an act of resistance against Tehran.Ramezanisadeh has now confirmed that the latter was the reason for her silence."We just wanted to stand with our people. I was scared at times, but I just tried to do what was right and say that no one should be killed just for protesting," Ramezanisadeh told Nine Network through an interpreter.She acknowledged the enormous personal risk involved in refusing to sing the anthem.Ramezanisadeh said her silence "could have meant any form of torture" for her."But at that moment, the only thing that gave me peace and a clear conscience was not singing it. I wanted to sing the anthem with pride and from my heart. But because of the situation in Iran, I really couldn't do it," she said.Pasandideh was equally direct about what motivated her."My people put their lives on the line and they were killed. Doing that was the absolute least we could do for them," Pasandideh said through an interpreter.The players' decision became even more significant after demonstrators in Australia called for the Iranian squad to be allowed to remain in the country rather than return home.The team eventually left Sydney on March 10, but the issue had already reached the highest levels of Australian politics.Australian Immigration Minister Tony Burke said the players had not been promised asylum when they made their decision."At that point, they had absolutely no information from us about the possibility of being able to stay," Burke said."The silence of itself was deeply significant," he added. "The reaction was the volcanic moment."The situation escalated further after then-US President Donald Trump publicly called for the Iranian players to be granted asylum and spoke to Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese about the issue.Albanese subsequently told Trump that four players and a team manager had accepted offers of humanitarian visas.Seven members of the Iranian delegation eventually accepted Australia's offer of asylum, but all except Ramezanisadeh and Pasandideh later changed their minds.The two women, meanwhile, decided to remain.Ramezanisadeh said the decision to stay in Australia came despite pressure from her parents, who urged her to return to Iran after receiving instructions from Iranian authorities."They tried to reassure me, saying: Nothing will happen to you. This is your home. You must return home.' But I told them my mind was made up and I was not coming back," she said.The decision has come at an enormous personal cost."Thinking that I might never be able to see my family again was heartbreaking, but I couldn't allow myself to be indifferent while so many young people were being killed by this regime. I couldn't stay silent, even though I miss my family so much," she added.Both players said they had not been in contact with their families in recent months, although they understood that their relatives had not been punished.Their decision to remain in Australia has also led to a new chapter in their football careers. Ramezanisadeh and Pasandideh now play for semi-professional club Wynnum Wolves in Brisbane and became Australian citizens in August.Pasandideh said she had deliberately avoided asking her former teammates whether they wanted to return to Iran or whether they felt compelled to do so."We decided not to talk because I don't want to put their lives in danger," she said.Despite everything that has happened, her attachment to Iran remains strong."One of my biggest dreams is to be able to go back to Iran, but in different circumstances when the situation in Iran has changed and the people of Iran are happy and thriving. Then I will go back and see my family," she added.
Article Summary: Iranian footballers Atefeh Ramezanisadeh and Fatemeh Pasandideh have broken their silence over the protest that preceded their decision to seek asylum in Australia. The two players, who abandoned the Iranian delegation after the tournament and remained in Australia, spoke publicly for the first time since claiming asylum. Their interview with Australia's 60 Minutes was broadcast on Sunday, shedding new light on a gesture that had sparked intense debate.

Article Title: ‘A long-time dream’: Nihal Sarin 'excited' but 'not thinking about' India's Chess Olympiad title defence
Article Text:
Nihal Sarin playing for American Gambits (GCL Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What happened in GCL on Day 2

BENGALURU: The Chess Olympiad is already on Indian Grandmaster Nihal Sarin’s mind, but not quite yet. With India preparing to defend its Open title in Samarkand, Uzbekistan later this month, Nihal is excited about representing the country at the Olympiad. For now, though, the 22-year-old is keeping his attention firmly on the Global Chess League (GCL), where he is representing American Gambits in this fourth season.Asked whether he was already thinking about the Olympiad while playing his games in Bengaluru, Nihal said: “Not really, no. Like, in general, I'm just extremely excited to play in the Olympiad. I'm very happy, and I'll just try to give my best for the team. It has been a long-time dream.”But with the GCL currently taking centre stage, Nihal is deliberately keeping things relaxed. “Now I'm just (focusing on GCL). This tournament is very relaxed. I'm just trying to chill on and off the board,” he said after American Gambits’ match against Ganges Grandmasters on Sunday.India’s title defence will carry considerable expectations. Four members of the Budapest-winning squad return, although there will understandably be significant changes to the board order.Arjun Erigaisi leads the five-player lineup on 2759, followed by Praggnanandhaa R on 2750. Nihal, rated 2718, will replace Pentala Harikrishna.World Champion Gukesh Dommaraju is also there, while Vidit Gujrathi completes the squad. Srinath Narayanan returns as captain.At the 2024 Olympiad in Budapest, Gukesh played on board one and delivered a phenomenal 9/10 score with a 3056 performance rating, winning individual gold as India finished four match points clear. Arjun also claimed individual gold on board three.Nevertheless, defending the title will be no easy task. Armenia remains the last team to successfully retain the Open crown, winning in 2006 and 2008. The last five editions have produced four different champions, underlining how difficult sustained dominance has been.Defending champions APL Pipers made it two wins from two, beating Ganges Grandmasters 11-6, while Ganges bounced back later to defeat American Gambits 9-7. Nihal won his game against Levon Aronian with black pieces in a nerve-wracking battle, but it was not enough for his team. Alaskan Knights beat Mumba Masters 11-6, before Mumba Masters edged Triveni Continental Kings 10-9 in the final match of the day.At this moment, American Gambits lead the standings on 6 match points and 31 game points, ahead of Ganges Grandmasters on 6/25. Alpine APL Pipers are third with 6/21, while Mumba Masters and Alaskan Knights have 3 match points each. Continental Kings, the two-time champions, remain at the bottom without a win.
Article Summary: Nihal Sarin is playing in the Global Chess League for American Gambits. The 22-year-old is excited about representing India at the Chess Olympiad. India will defend its Open title in Samarkand, Uzbekistan later this month. Nihal will replace Pentala Harikrishna.

Article Title: Satwik-Chirag breach Great Wall, China Masters win boosts Asian Games hopes
Article Text:
Indian men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, right, and Chirag Shetty clinch the China Masters Super 750 title. (PTI Photo)

‘We’ll go all guns blazing’

Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, right, and Chirag Shetty (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

As Chirag Shetty ’s winning shot landed in the middle of the court, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy let himself go — breaking into his trademark single-leg dance, arms swinging and a broad smile lighting up his face. A delighted Chirag flung his T-shirt into the stands.Sunday, it turned out, needed to see them fall behind before it could watch them fly. The Indian duo fought back to beat China’s He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu 11-21, 21-13, 21-17 in a pulsating final in Shenzhen.For a pair that has spent most of the last four years battling injuries as much as they did opponents, the title was more than just another trophy. It was a statement — and perhaps a timely reminder that the old Satwik-Chirag swagger is returning.Satwik Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty on Sunday became the first Indian shuttlers to win the China Masters BWF Super 750 title, and the timing could hardly have been better. With the Asian Games title defence looming later this month, the China Masters crown gives the pair exactly what they needed: belief, momentum and proof that the long road back from injury is beginning to lead somewhere familiar.“Obviously, going into the Asian Games, winning a title definitely gives a huge boost.We’ll go back home, push our- selves to the limit, train for the next 10 days and go all guns blazing at the Asian Games. We want to go out there and have some fun,” Chirag said later.Playing their third final at this tour- nament, the Indians were far from their best at the start. They were outplayed in the opening game, unable to match the pace and aggression of the Chinese pair. But just as they have done so often in their partnership, they found a way back. Even in the decider, they were staring at trou- ble at 3-7. But then came the shift.The Indians began slowing the rallies down, keeping the shuttle below the tape and refusing to allow the Chinese to un- leash their explosive attacking game. Chirag moved closer to the net, taking control of the forecourt, while Satwik found greater rhythm from the back. The comeback was on. From 16-17, the Indians produced a five-point burst that changed the complexion of the final and left the home pair with no answer.It was a finish that had been written into their script long before Sunday.“Playing here is always good. We have al- ways played here coming back from inju- ry,” a breathless Satwik later said.“I think in 2024, after the Olympics, we played here and reached the semifinals. Then last year, we played the final, though we weren’t in very good shape. I think this is also, after coming back from injury, a tournament that has given us a lot of con- fidence,” he explained.It was also a victory that vindicated the faith of their coach Kim Tan Her, who had felt Satwik was beginning to redis- cover his best after his latest injury layoff.The first game, however, gave little in- dication of what was to follow. The Indi- ans lost 11-21, struggling to impose them- selves and repeatedly allowing the Chi- nese to dictate the pace.Kim knew something had to change.“I told them to control the net and asked Chirag to stay up front and take control of the rallies. The Chinese are playing real- ly well, so we needed to counter that by locking one player at the front. It’s a great victory for them, especially with the Asian Games coming,” Kim told TOI.The message was simple: take away the Chinese attack before it gathers mo- mentum. Chirag admitted they had played into the hands of their opponents in the opening game. “I think we were not playing the right strokes. We were play- ing a style which favoured them. And when we play a style which favours them, they come all guns blazing,” he said.The China Masters, which had twice seen the Indians leave without the title — semifinalists in 2024 and runners-up last year — had finally been conquered.
Article Summary: Indian men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty clinch the China Masters Super 750 title. The Indian duo fought back to beat China’s He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu 11-21, 21-13,21-17 in a pulsating final in Shenzhen.

Article Title: Duleep Trophy final: Ishan Kishan fires after Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s cameo, puts East on solid footing
Article Text:
East Zone's captain Ishan Kishan celebrates his century on day 1 of the Duleep Trophy final. (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BRIEF SCORES:

CHENNAI: There was a good Sunday crowd at the MA Chidambaram Stadium to watch teen sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi fire. They got a glimpse of it, but it was Ishan Kishan who stole the show on the opening day of the Duleep Trophy final here on Sunday.After Sooryavanshi enthralled in the first hour with a breezy 37-ball 44 taking apart Mohammed Siraj, Kishan, batting at No. 5, struck his 10th firstclass century, remaining unbeaten on 111 off 135 balls (14x4, 1x6), to put his side firmly in command against South Zone. Kishan, who is currently out of India’s red-ball set-up, made the most of the easy batting conditions and tiring South attack on a hot day as East Zone closed at 385-4 in 79 overs.Kishan, who reached his half-century off 71 balls, accelerated after reaching the milestone, bringing up his second fifty in just 51 balls. He completed his century off 122 balls, driving veteran leggie Shreyas Gopal, playing his 100th First-Class match, straight down the ground for a boundary.He was given excellent support by right-hander Kumar Kushagra, who is unbeaten on 63 off 75 balls (4x4, 5x6). The pair stitched an unbeaten 144-run fifth-wicket partnership, leaving East Zone in a commanding position.Earlier, after Kishan won the toss and opted to bat, all eyes were on Sooryavanshi. The teenager did not take long to entertain, smashing two boundaries off MD Nidhees in the sixth over, one off the front foot and another off the back foot, both through the cover region.He then took on Siraj, hitting the pacer for a boundary and a six over long-off before dispatching the final ball of the over for another four. With East Zone racing to 50 in just 7.5 overs, South skipper Tilak Varma was forced to introduce off-spinner Tripurana Vijay, who extracted sharp turn with his first delivery.South employed a defensive field for the 15-year-old, with five fielders stationed outside the ring on the leg and off sides, which is unusual so early in a five-day game.Siraj endured an expensive opening spell, conceding 41 runs in five overs. East Zone reached 70-0 in 10 overs and then 100 in 14.3 overs. Abhimanyu Easwaran (72 off 86 balls) matched Sooryavanshi’s aggression and brought up his 50 in 46 balls.However, the opening stand was broken at 100 when Chama Milind (2-56) dismissed Sooryavanshi for 44 off 37 balls. The youngster attempted to pull a short delivery but mistimed it, with substitute Tanay Thyagarajan completing the catch running in from deep square leg. Easwaran looked extremely assured and seemed set for a century, but was run out.East Zone 385-4 (Easwaran 72, Mohan 85, Kishan 111*, Kushagra 63*; C Milind 2-56) vs South.
Article Summary: East Zone captain Ishan Kishan scores 111 in Duleep Trophy final. Teen sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi fires 44 in first hour. East Zone close day one of final at 385-4 in 79 overs. Kumar Kushagra and Abhimanyu Easwaran add 144-run fifth- wicket partnership.

Article Title: TOI Exclusive: Personal coaches push gains momentum in equestrian, selectors’ dual roles raise questions
Article Text:
Ashish Limaye (TOI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With the Asian Games barely weeks away, a curious battle over coaches is brewing in Indian equestrian — five riders have sought accreditation for their foreign personal coaches, even as officials involved in selecting the team are themselves headed to Japan in coaching and team-management roles.The demand has put the spotlight on how the equestrian contingent’s coaching support was finalised, particularly because the foreign coaches being sought by the riders have trained them through the international season and are now being preferred over some of the Indian coaches cleared by the sports authorities.TOI has learnt that at least five of the seven dressage and eventing riders have sought to take their personal coaches to the Games. The five are Shruti Vora (athlete) — Rebecca Moody (British, coach); Ashish Limaye — Carola Bierlein (German); Gaurav Pundir — Brian Barnett (Dutch); Arjan Nagra — Felix Etzel (German); and Jai Sud — Antonie de Ridder (Dutch).All five have approached the Indian Olympic Association (IOA)-run ad-hoc committee for governance of the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), seeking accreditation for their personal coaches.The issue gets more intriguing when viewed alongside the composition of the selection committees. Documents accessed by TOI show Col Sandeep Dewan, Jai Rathore (who also goes by the name Mrityunjay Sinh Rathore and Jay Rathore) and Kapil Modi were on the dressage selection committee, while Col Amit Sinsinwar and Imitiaz Anees were on the three-day eventing selection committee. Dewan and Imitiaz were also part of the technical committee.Several of these officials are now travelling with the contingent. The sanctioned coaching/support staff included Anees, Rathore and Sinsinwar as coaches, with Dewan as team leader.Sources said the overlap between those involved in selecting the Asian Games team and those accompanying it has raised questions about a potential conflict of interest, though there is no suggestion of wrongdoing against any individual.The issue is particularly pointed in Shruti’s case. Sources said the dressage rider has written to the authorities stating that Rathore has not coached her and that she has been trained by Moody. She has sought Moody’s accreditation instead.There is also the Sinsinwar episode. India’s show jumping squad was dropped after failing to meet the selection criteria, leaving the country to compete only in dressage and three-day eventing. Yet Sinsinwar, nominated as show jumping coach, was initially included in the sanctioned contingent.The anomaly was subsequently corrected. In a mail accessed by TOI, the IOA told EFI’s ad-hoc committee that Sinsinwar was “not to be deputed to Japan” as the show jumping team had not been approved, and directed that his accreditation card be returned.The personal-coach issue, however, remains alive.In the same communication, the IOA said it was “taking the necessary steps” with the OCA and AINAGOC regarding the five personal coaches and getting them accreditation.Interestingly, EFI’s ad-hoc committee had separately recommended just two — Moody and Bierlein — saying they could also coach other members of the team.The questions now are hard to ignore: why were coaches sought by riders not part of the original support structure, why are officials involved in selection also travelling with the team, and was the initial coaching list the result of oversight — or simply the federation’s recommendation being accepted without enough scrutiny?
Article Summary: Five riders have sought accreditation for their foreign personal coaches. Officials involved in selecting the team are themselves headed to Japan in coaching and team-management roles. The demand has put the spotlight on how the equestrian contingent’s coaching support was finalised.

Article Title: ‘Sindarov’s chance to shock Carlsen’: Experts feel Uzbek GM will have to seize his moments
Article Text:
Javokhir Sindarov

Results:

BENGALURU: The wait for the big match between Magnus Carlsen and Javokhir Sindarov in the Global Chess League (GCL) will end on Monday, when the two giants clash on the icon board.The much-awaited clash occurs in the GCL version of rapid chess, which has no increments for the first 40 moves, and is more likely to produce a winner. The chess world is eagerly awaiting the clash between them — there will be at least two in this edition — and top players consider Carlsen as the overwhelming favourite. The two will clash when APL Pipers take on American Gambits in the third match of the day.“For Sindarov, this match is to prove that he is up there and ready to take on Magnus. Whereas, Magnus looked chilled out and I don’t think he is thinking too much about this particular game. He just wants to play good chess and show that he is still the No. 1 and the best ever,” Bengaluru GM Pranav Anand told TOI.“I was following Magnus’ match against Maxime,” the 19-year-old said. “I think Magnus starts as the overwhelming favourite. Sindarov has good chances but I don’t see him beating Magnus. Most likely, it’s going to end in a draw.” Pranav also felt Monday’s match would be Sindarov's best chance.“Magnus starts playing his best chess in the second half of the tournament. He will just start winning continuously in that phase. He is a bit sloppy in the first few rounds, so Monday’s match is Sindarov’s best chance.”Alpine APL Pipers bt Ganges Grandmasters 11-6, Mumba Masters lost to Alaskan Knights 6-11, Ganges bt American Gambits 9-7; Continental Kings lost to Mumba Masters 9-10.
Article Summary: Magnus Carlsen and Javokhir Sindarov will clash on the icon board on Monday. The much-awaited clash occurs in the GCL version of rapid chess, which has no increments for the first 40 moves. The chess world is eagerly awaiting the clash between them.

Article Title: Hockey World Cup high over, India women chase gold at Asian Games
Article Text:
India women's hockey team (ANI Photo)

BENGALURU: Barely a week after finishing fifth at the FIH World Cup in Belgium, Salima Tete and her teammates were back at the SAI South Centre here, preparing for their biggest assignment of the year — the Asian Games starting in Japan on Sept 19.With little time between the two competitions, the Indian women’s hockey team has hardly had a chance to savour or celebrate an impressive World Cup campaign. “I just got a text from a friend asking about the celebrations, given we did well at the World Cup. But the celebrations have to wait. We can enjoy afterwards. Things are going very fast, and we have to move on to the next one,” chief coach Sjoerd Marijne said.The focus now, the Dutchman added, is on building on their World Cup performance. “We paused and reflected on what we achieved. I told the girls to be very proud of what we’ve done. But we need to go further and do better than at the World Cup. What we did there may not be enough at the Asian Games. They need to stay focused,” he said.Striker Lalremsiami summed up the intensity of the turnaround, revealing that the players have not even had time for a cheat meal since returning to training. “We can’t afford to have a cheatmeal day now,” she quipped.India won bronze at the previous edition of the Asian Games and had to take the qualifier route to secure their place at the Paris Olympics. This time, with an Olympic berth for the 2028 Los Angeles Games at stake, nothing less than gold will be the target.“I know the expectations are higher. We are a very strong contender for gold. But before the gold medal, we need to win other matches. That’s why we must give our best every day. Of course, you go into a tournament to achieve the highest reward, and that is an Olympic berth,” Marijne said.
Article Summary: India finished fifth at the FIH World Cup in Belgium. The Asian Games starts in Japan on Sept 19. India won bronze at the previous edition of the Asian Games and had to take the qualifier route to secure their place at the Paris Olympics.

Article Title: Vishesh Sharma fights off tough conditions to win Golconda Masters on home course
Article Text:
Telangana Golconda Masters: Vishesh Sharma wins maiden title on home course. (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Two days after lifting the Golconda Masters trophy at the Hyderabad Golf Association (HGA), 19-year old Vishesh Sharma reflected on a victory that was shaped by home support, demanding course conditions and the realities of pursuing professional golf in India as a self-funded athlete.The Golconda Masters is one of the marquee events on the PGTI calendar. Vishesh’s consistency across changing conditions proved decisive as he emerged on top in a tightly contested field.“The greens were phenomenal and rolling at great speeds. The rough was up as usual, so it’s always quite a challenge around the greens,” Vishesh said. “The showers made the course play differently almost every day, so all of us had to adapt and strategise accordingly.”Although familiar with HGA, he believes the biggest advantage came not from local knowledge but from the people walking alongside him.“What was special for me this week was having my friends, family and my coach there supporting me throughout. I think that was one of the key things that helped me secure this win,” he said.The title is another significant step in the 19-year-old’s steady rise on the PGTI, but his journey has been far from glamorous.Vishesh funds his own career, managing travel and equipment.His introduction to golf was almost accidental. Growing up in Vadodara, where his father worked as a govt officer, the family took a membership at the Gaekwad Baroda Golf Club primarily for recreational activities.“We used to go there for swimming, tennis and other activities. Golf happened coincidentally. I started going to the course, played a couple of junior events and gradually got into the sport,” he recalled.That gradual progression has also shaped his perspective on success and failure. “I wouldn’t say there’s one particular week because in golf, every week teaches us something. Whether it’s a win or whether we miss the cut, we learn more about ourselves and how we can get better,” he said.The standard of Indian golf has risen noticeably this season, with stronger fields and increased prize purses following the DP World Tour’s partnership with the PGTI. “DP World being our umbrella partner doesn’t just help financially. The name itself carries a certain weight and gives players confidence to go out there and show that we can compete,” he said.Even with constant travel across the country, his preparation remains remarkably consistent. Together with his coach, Vishesh follows a structured practice routine before every event, modifying only the finer details to suit each venue.With the Golconda Masters title secured, Vishesh has reinforced his place among PGTI’s in-form golfers while underlining the determination required to succeed in a demanding individual sport.
Article Summary: Vishesh Sharma won the Telangana Golconda Masters at the Hyderabad Golf Association. The 19-year-old is a self-funded professional golfer in India. Vishesh says the biggest advantage came from his friends and family.

Article Title: Wiser, more social Elavenil Valarivan ready for the Asian Games challenge
Article Text:
Elavenil Valarivan (Image credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PUNE: Elavenil Valarivan is just 27, but she is already one of the ‘oldest’ shooters in India’s team for the Asian Games With two Olympics, more than a dozen of World Cups, World Championships and Asian Championships and nine years of shooting under her name, she is certainly the richest in terms of experience. And yet, the Ahmedabad shooter will be excited as a fresher when she takes aim at the 10m air rifle competitions at the Asian Games in Nagoya-Aich, Japan, later this month.Elavenil, who had missed the bus for the 2023 edition of the Asian Games, is happy to be back for the continental Games. “I’m grateful to be a part of the Asian Games again. I’m very excited to participate as 2025 and 2026 have been pleasant years for me. I’ve been pretty satisfied with myself so I’m just looking forward to doing the absolute same thing and being myself,” the Tokyo and Paris Games participant told TOI during the national camp in Bhopal.Elavenil had heartbreaks in the two Olympic participations, but the shooter feels disappointment is bound to happen as so much ride on the quadrennial Games.“The Olympics are different because it’s once in four years and it is the most celebrated sporting tournament in the world. You have expectations, and no matter how much you say, ‘No, no, I don’t have any expectations’, at the end of the day, you know it is important to you, and that’s where the expectations arise,” she said.Born to Tamil parents, Elavenil grew up in Ahmedabad and started shooting when she was 13. Since then, she was tuned to win medals. But now, she just doesn’t chase medals.“At Tokyo I was a young athlete. Coping with the Tokyo disappointment was something that took all my energy. That learning helped me for Paris. After Paris, I think my perspective has changed. Till Paris, it was about winning the medal. Now, it is more about enjoying the sport, and the results are showing,” Elavenil said.The rifle shooter has also made friends off the range.“Last year my brother got married and he was busy with his life so I really wanted to have a life of my own. I started going to social gatherings. Fortunately, I met such amazing people. And the best thing is, none of them are in sports,” she said.
Article Summary: Elavenil Valarivan is one of the 'oldest' shooters in India’s team for the Asian Games. The 27-year-old shooter will compete in the 10m air rifle competitions. Elavenil had heartbreaks in the two Olympic participations, but feels disappointment is bound to happen as so much ride on the quadrennial Games.

Article Title: Govt crossing line in RCA politics: Ashok Gehlot
Article Text:
Former cricketer Vinod Mathur (left), former CM Ashok Gehlot and MLA Rafeeq Khan (right) felicitate Kushagra Ojha at the 33rd Mathura Das Mathur Awards on Sunday.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

JAIPUR: Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot launched a scathing attack on the BJP govt, raising severe concerns over political interference in the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) and accusing the state administration of derailing major infrastructure projects, including the international stadium at Chonp.Expressing anguish over the persistent administrative crisis in the state’s cricket body, Gehlot lamented the lack of international cricket action in the capital. “Unfortunately, for the past five years, no international matches are being hosted here anymore. This should be a matter of concern,” the veteran Congress leader said, taking aim at the govt over the prolonged governance vacuum.It was in Nov 2021, under the tenure of his son Vaibhav Gehlot as RCA president, that the Sawai Man Singh Stadium last hosted an international fixture — a T20I between India and New Zealand.Speaking as the chief guest at the 33rd Mathura Das Mathur Awards on Sunday, Gehlot felicitated upcoming state cricketers across sub-junior, junior and senior categories.His remarks come against the backdrop of unprecedented turmoil within the RCA. The association has been managed by govt-appointed ad hoc committees, which have seen intense internal power struggles, factional rivalries and failure to conduct democratic elections.Hitting out at the BJP dispensation for crossing limits in sports administration, Gehlot added, “The politics going on in cricket is very painful. Rajasthan’s history is deeply linked with cricket. Politics happens everywhere nowadays; it even happens in the judiciary. It happens everywhere, in every field. It happens in sports associations as well. But it should not be to the extent that sports and sports associations suffer. Such politics, I believe, should not happen. A line should not be crossed. Now, the govt itself is crossing that line.”Gehlot particularly targeted the delay in holding RCA elections. “It has been three years for this govt, and so far, there is no news about RCA elections. Ad hoc panels have been formed. Such a situation existing at the government level is, I believe, painful,” he remarked, urging chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma to respect the youth’s passion for cricket and facilitate immediate elections.Comparing his tenure’s initiatives, such as the creation of the Barkatullah Khan Stadium in Jodhpur, 2% sports reservation in govt jobs, and the Rural/Urban Olympics, with the current administration, Gehlot asserted that the BJP govt has failed on sports commitments.He highlighted the stalled progress of the world-class Chonp Stadium, envisioned during Vaibhav’s tenure as RCA president in collaboration with industrialist Anil Agarwal. “When CP Joshi and Vaibhav were there, we had a talk with Anil Agarwal... He promised to give Rs 250 to Rs 300 crore. I heard he even gave Rs 100 to Rs 150 crore,” Gehlot noted, calling on the state govt to engage with Vedant Group’s chairperson to resume the construction of the facility.Gehlot concluded that key public infrastructure across the state, from cricket stadiums to the FinTech Institute and IPD Tower, has faced unnecessary delays under the current regime, calling for immediate corrective action in public interest.
Article Summary: Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot spoke at the 33rd Mathura Das Mathur Awards on Sunday. He expressed anguish over the persistent administrative crisis in the state’s cricket body. He highlighted the stalled progress of the world-class Chonp Stadium.

Article Title: Gen Next sets the pace: Four young women fast bowlers eye India selection after 13,000-strong talent hunt
Article Text:
AKSHITA BHAGAT

JOSHNA ANGEL

PALAK SINGH

ROHITA CHOWDRY

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Sometimes, all it takes to unlock talent is a spark. It can come from within or from someone willing to light it for you. For Akshita Bhagat, Palak Singh, Rohita Chowdry and Joshna Angel, the WPL Speed Queen initiative provided that spark.The four were among more than 13,000 aspirants who registered for the talent hunt. Around 7,500 made it to the trials before 56 finalists showcased their speed, strength and ambition at the finale in Mumbai earlier this year. Their performances have since opened another door.Having earned the opportunity to train under some of the best coaches and observe some of the finest cricketers at the BCCI Centre of Excellence, the four fast bowlers are now aiming higher. They are currently training under coach Krishna Kumar at CoE. TOI takes a look at the future India prospects...The first to make the big leap is Mohali teenager Akshita. The 19-year old was last month named in the India ‘A’ one-day squad for the upcoming home series against Australia ‘A’, a significant step in a journey that began with gully cricket.Akshita joined has represented Punjab in national age-group and senior domestic tournaments.She started out as a batter before switching to pace bowling and counts India captain Harmanpreet Kaur among her role models. For her, Speed Queen provided the exposure and belief to accelerate that journey.“There were a lot of learnings from the Speed Queen and the camp here has furthered that. The coaches worked on our tactics and basics. I learned what I can improve, what I need to work on and, more importantly, learnt the importance of hard work. Also, being around established players has allowed me to pick their brains,” said Akshita, a huge fan of former South African pacer Dale Steyn and Australian great Ellyse Perry.With a senior India camp now in her sights, Akshita feels the CoE experience has been defining. “I didn’t expect to come to the CoE so soon, where you get the best strength and conditioning facilities and coaches. When I started, the dream was to play for India, but I didn’t think I would take such a huge step towards it so soon,” she said.At 15, Joshna is a pocket dynamo — petite and bubbly off the field, fierce and fast with a ball in hand. The Chennai teenager clocked 108 kmph during the trials. Her introduction to both the sport and bowling came from her father, R Jesuraj, a former Tamil Nadu medium pacer.Joshna took up cricket out of boredom during the Covid-19 lockdown. She is now dreaming big. “The Speed Queen program helped me gain confidence and get to know my strengths,” said Joshna, who has represented Tamil Nadu in the U-15 and U-19 categories.Her father remains one of her inspirations, along with England pacer Lauren Bell. The CoE camp, meanwhile, has opened her eyes to the demands of elite sport. “One of the key lessons has been how to stay focused and be sincere in maintaining the diet. There has also been a lot of emphasis on exercising, which has taught me a lot,” she said.Meeting India internationals Tilak Varma and Sanju Samson has been another highlight. As for the ultimate goal, there was no hesitation. “I want to play for India,” she declared boldly.Athletics was Palak’s first calling. Cricket, however, was the sport her father chose for her. Three years after taking up the game, the 15-year old has already shown that she can generate serious pace. She clocked 108 kmph in the zonal trials and 106 kmph in the finale. Inspired by Australian fast bowler Mitchell Starc, Palak is now learning to make the most of her height while understanding that pace is only one part of the equation.“Coming here is a big thing. It’s a very good opportunity and a valuable experience to train under some of the best coaches in the country. I have understood my bowling better, and I now know that a bowler should also have accuracy, consistency, swing and variations,” she said.Having cut her teeth in the state age group team, Palak now has a more immediate target: breaking into the India U-19 side. “From here, I will get a good pathway to play for India in the future. I am only 15, so I have the India U-19 team to look ahead to,” she said.Rohita’s journey to pace bowling began on the track. A former heptathlete, the Bengaluru youngster took up cricket at her father’s insistence. Given her athleticism and natural speed, fast bowling was an obvious fit.The 24-year old has represented various Karnataka teams but was going through a difficult phase before the Speed Queen opportunity came her way. “I was going struggling to make my place in the senior Karnataka team. I was hesitant to even participate in the event. But because of it, I regained a lot of confidence; it came as a ray of hope,” said Rohita, who clocked 109 kmph in the initial round before touching 104 kmph in the finale.The CoE experience has since given that confidence another boost. “This is what dreams are made of. Bumping into international cricketers and learning from their process has been crucial. I’ve learnt that there is so much more to just bowling fast. There’s so much that goes into our nutrition, fitness training and running programmes,” she said.Rohita, who holds a degree in international relations, public policy and journalism, always had the backing of her parents. She draws inspiration from Jhulan Goswami’s longevity and says a conversation with CoE head of cricket VVS Laxman has been one of the highlights of the camp.
Article Summary: Akshita Bhagat, Palak Singh, Rohita Chowdry and Joshna Angel were part of the WPL Speed Queen initiative. The four were among more than 13,000 aspirants who registered for the talent hunt. Around 7,500 made it to the trials before 56 finalists showcased their speed, strength and ambition at the finale in Mumbai.

Article Title: ‘Cosmetic surgery’ won’t fix Pakistan cricket: Misbah-ul-Haq takes aim at PCB after stepping down
Article Text:
Misbah ul Haq (AFP Photo)

Misbah alleges double standards

'We shouldn't panic'

Misbah points to India's model

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan Test captain Misbah-ul-Haq has criticised the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) for what he described as a reactive approach to handling the national team, following the decision to send seven players and two coaches back home during the ongoing Test tour of England.Misbah, who recently resigned as Pakistan’s national selector, stepped down shortly after the PCB announced its decision earlier this week. The development came after the board issued show-cause notices to every member of the selection committee.The PCB’s decision saw head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul released from the Test squad, while seven players were also removed. Pakistan subsequently sent its white-ball players to England for the final match of the series.Speaking on a television show, Misbah questioned the way local coaches are treated compared with their foreign counterparts in Pakistan cricket.According to the former captain, overseas coaches are given greater authority while facing considerably less scrutiny when results do not go their way."It is a fact that local and foreign coaches are treated differently in Pakistan cricket. Local coaches have to face more scrutiny and criticism when compared to foreign coaches," he said.Misbah made it clear that his criticism was not directed at the appointment of overseas coaches themselves. Instead, he argued that the wider cricketing ecosystem tends to give foreign coaches an easier ride."I don't think there is anything wrong in having foreign coaches but what bothers me is we (fans, critics, media, PCB) tend to have a soft corner for foreign coaches," he added.He further explained that the imbalance extends to the level of responsibility placed on coaches."We tend to give foreign coaches more authority and power and he is held less responsible if the team performs poorly. In contrast, local coaches always facing scrutiny from everyone."Misbah also took aim at the PCB’s decision-making process, warning that sudden changes made under pressure could create more problems for a team already in need of stability.He argued that Pakistan cannot afford to repeatedly overhaul its setup without first conducting a proper assessment of performances and identifying the reasons behind its struggles."We shouldn't panic and do cosmetic surgery because of pressure. We need to analyse performances and the situation and then decide how to move forward," Misbah said.The former selector added: "Unfortunately, we are used to taking reactive decisions in Pakistan cricket."For Misbah, the solution requires patience and a long-term strategy rather than immediate responses to poor results.The former Pakistan captain also compared the country's cricketing structure with India's, highlighting the gradual development of the Indian system since the 1990s.He pointed to Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli as examples from the Indian setup and argued that India's success against Pakistan has been helped by greater exposure and stronger preparation for pressure situations."Our youngsters are playing too much white-ball cricket and their exposure to red-ball cricket is limited. Not enough four-day cricket. This means they have more chances of cracking under pressure."India took time to process and develop and they made gradual investments in their system after the 90s. There is no quick fix to the system."Misbah's comments come at a turbulent time for Pakistan cricket, with the PCB making major changes to the Test setup even before the England tour has concluded. His message, however, was that lasting improvement will require consistency, greater red-ball exposure for young players and sustained investment rather than repeated reactions to short-term setbacks.
Article Summary: Misbah-ul-Haq criticises Pakistan Cricket Board for'reactive' approach. Former captain questions the way local coaches are treated compared with foreign counterparts in Pakistan cricket. Misbah compares Pakistan's cricketing structure with India's, highlighting the gradual development of the Indian system.

Article Title: Jordan Hermann, bowlers shine as South Africa beat Zimbabwe to clinch tri-series title
Article Text:
Jordan Hermann (Image credit: X)

Hermann gives South Africa a flying start

Zimbabwe lose wickets early

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Evans fights back but Zimbabwe fall short

Important preparation for 2027 World Cup

South Africa produced a strong all-round performance to beat Zimbabwe by 48 runs in the final and win the T20I tri-series at the Namibia Cricket Ground on Sunday.Batting first, South Africa posted 205/5 in 20 overs after choosing to bat. Jordan Hermann led the way with a quick half-century, while Dewald Brevis and Rubin Hermann also made important contributions.Zimbabwe struggled from the start in the chase and were bowled out for 157 in 18 overs.South Africa were without opener Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who missed the final with a niggle. But his absence did not affect the team's start.Jordan Hermann attacked the Zimbabwe bowlers from the beginning and reached his fifty in just 24 balls. His innings included eight fours and a six.He added 84 runs for the opening wicket with Connor Esterhuizen, who scored 32.Brevis then kept the pressure on Zimbabwe in the middle overs. He scored 32 from 23 balls, hitting two fours and two sixes.Rubin Hermann added 27 off 16 balls, with three fours and a six. His partnership with Brevis helped South Africa cross the 200-run mark.Brad Evans and Newman Nyamhuri took two wickets each for Zimbabwe, but South Africa finished with a big total of 205/5.Zimbabwe needed 206 runs to win but suffered a terrible start.Ben Curran was dismissed for a first-ball duck by Eathan Bosch. Duan Jansen and Bosch then continued to trouble the Zimbabwe batters as four wickets fell inside the powerplay.Captain Sikandar Raza got a second chance when a caught-behind decision against him was overturned because Bosch had bowled a no-ball.However, South Africa captain Bjorn Fortuin soon ended Raza's stay at the crease. He finished with three wickets for 24 runs as Zimbabwe's chase fell apart.Brad Evans gave Zimbabwe some hope late in the innings.The pacer scored his maiden T20I half-century and put on 52 runs for the ninth wicket with Kundai Matigimu.But Kwena Maphaka broke the partnership, and Zimbabwe were eventually bowled out in the 18th over.Duan Jansen was South Africa's best bowler, finishing with 3/38, while Bosch took 2/22.It was South Africa's third win over Zimbabwe in just eight days.The tri-series was an important preparation tournament for South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, who will co-host the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup.South Africa will now play a three-match ODI series against Namibia. Fortuin will continue to lead the team in the series.
Article Summary: South Africa beat Zimbabwe by 48 runs in the final of the T20I tri-series. South Africa posted 205/5 in 20 overs after choosing to bat. Jordan Hermann led the way with a quick half-century. Dewald Brevis and Rubin Hermann also made important contributions.

Article Title: 'Bhaiya gave me a lot of advice': Shikhar Mohan’s 85 gives East Zone a lift; Reveals Ishan Kishan’s guidance
Article Text:
Young Jharkhand batter Shikhar Mohan (IANS Image)

Ranji form and T20 experience boost debut

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Shikhar Mohan, Jharkhand batter credited captain Ishan Kishan ’s constant guidance after making an impressive 85 on his Duleep Trophy debut against South Zone in the 2026/27 final.Mohan, who came into the East Zone XI as a replacement for Jharkhand teammate Virat Singh, played a key role in rebuilding the innings after the early wickets. He added 94 runs for the third wicket with Kishan, helping East Zone recover and take control on the opening day.Kishan remained unbeaten on 111 at stumps, while Kumar Kushagra was not out on 63 as East Zone finished the day on 385/4 in 79 overs.“Ishan bhaiya was giving me a lot of advice while batting. He was telling me what shot is on and what is not. Thanks to that, we had a great partnership,” Mohan told reporters after play.Mohan earned his place in the East Zone side after an outstanding debut Ranji Trophy season, where he scored 613 runs at an average of 55.72. Although primarily an opener, he had no issues adapting to the No. 3 position with Abhimanyu Easwaran and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi opening for East Zone.“My journey has been very good so far. My first season in Ranji Trophy went very well, so coming into this match, I just wanted to carry that forward.I was looking to maintain that form from the Ranji Trophy,” he said.Mohan also accepted the challenge of facing South Zone’s short-ball strategy, with five fielders stationed on the leg side. He showed patience before eventually falling to Chama Milind after an inside edge off a bouncer.“The plan was that I would leave the ball first, and when they get tired, they will give me chances to score runs. I made a poor decision and got out,” he admitted.The youngster also felt his experience in the Jharkhand T20 League helped him handle the pressure of playing in front of a sizeable crowd at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.“I think it helped a lot. The crowds there were also very good, so today when there was a big crowd, it felt normal to me,” Mohan said.
Article Summary: Jharkhand's Shikhar Mohan scores 85 on debut in Duleep Trophy final. East Zone captain Ishan Kishan remains unbeaten on 111 at stumps. Mohan came into the East Zone XI as a replacement for Jharkshand teammate Virat Singh.

Article Title: Title-chasing Nottinghamshire lose Kyle Verreynne ahead of crucial County Championship run-in
Article Text:
South Africa's Kyle Verreynne (PTI Photo)

Verreynne departure comes at crucial stage

Mick Newell acknowledges CSA’s decision

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nottinghamshire’s County Championship title push has suffered a blow after South Africa wicketkeeper-batter Kyle Verreynne was recalled early by Cricket South Africa, ruling him out of the club’s final three matches of the season.Verreynne, 29, is in his third stint with Nottinghamshire and had initially agreed to play in all of the club’s red-ball fixtures this summer. However, his central contract commitments with South Africa take priority as the Proteas prepare for a three-Test home series against Australia.His final appearance for Nottinghamshire this season will come against Leicestershire at Trent Bridge, before he returns to South Africa.Verreynne’s departure comes at a crucial stage of Nottinghamshire’s campaign. They currently sit second in the County Championship, four points behind leaders Somerset and one point ahead of third-placed Warwickshire, with just three rounds remaining.The club will now have to manage the final stretch of the title race without their first-choice wicketkeeper, with fixtures against Hampshire, Sussex and Yorkshire still to come.Despite his early departure, Verreynne said he would continue to follow Nottinghamshire’s title challenge closely.“I think I've said it so many times, the club's got a really special place. It's got a special place to me, so I'll be watching closely.”He added:“The team's in a good position at the moment, playing some really good cricket. I think it's going to be quite an exciting run-in, so I'll be keeping a close eye.”Nottinghamshire Director of Cricket Mick Newell admitted that losing Verreynne at this point of the season was far from ideal, although the club understood South Africa’s position.“It’s not ideal that we’re losing Kyle at this point in the season, but we understand the decision made by Cricket South Africa, and he returns with our best wishes for a busy winter.”Newell also praised Verreynne’s contribution during his latest spell with the club, saying his performances had helped Nottinghamshire put themselves in a strong position heading into the final weeks of the Championship.“We’ve been very happy to have Kyle with us for most of the summer, during which his contributions have put us in a strong position as we head towards the final few matches,” he said.With several South African players being recalled from county cricket ahead of the Australia series, Nottinghamshire will now look for a replacement for Verreynne.“There’s always a lot of hard work being done behind the scenes to make sure we’re prepared for every outcome, and we hope to confirm a replacement for Kyle as soon as we’re able to,” Newell added.
Article Summary: South Africa wicketkeeper-batter Kyle Verreynne has been recalled early by Cricket South Africa. The 29-year-old had agreed to play in all of Nottinghamshire's red-ball fixtures this summer. However, his central contract commitments with South Africa take priority as the Proteas prepare for a three- Test home series against Australia. His final appearance for Nottinghamshire will come against Leicestershire.

Article Title: 'Land has been allotted': Tripura CM fulfils promise to CWG medallist Asmita Dey
Article Text:
India's Asmita Dey (PTI Photo)

From a village in Tripura to Commonwealth Games glory

CM urges Asmita to target Asian Games success

NEW DELHI: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey, with the state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house.The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.Dey won the women’s -48kg title in Glasgow after defeating Canada’s Heidi Quach in a dramatic golden-score contest. The state government also presented her with a cheque of Rs 10 lakh as part of the felicitation.Speaking at the event, Saha highlighted Dey’s difficult journey from a small village in South Tripura to the top of the Commonwealth Games podium. Her father, he noted, worked as a cycle mechanic in Sonaichari.“The journey from an obscure village in South Tripura to a podium finish at Glasgow was a race against time. Her father was a cycle mechanic at Sonaichari. Against all odds, she stood firm on her mission and achieved phenomenal success for the country,” he said.The chief minister recalled meeting Dey at Tripura Bhavan in New Delhi after her return from the Games.During that meeting, the judoka had expressed her wish to have a house in Agartala.“During the meeting, Asmita revealed she desperately wanted a house in Agartala. I promised to fulfil her wish, and today a piece of land has been allotted to her,” he said.Saha said Dey’s achievement could motivate more young athletes from Tripura to pursue sport at the highest level. He also urged her to remain disciplined as she prepares for the Asian Games, particularly because of the strict anti-doping requirements.“I urge Asmita to remain alert, particularly about food, because she has to pass through a stringent dope test before joining the prestigious Asian Games. We believe she will shine again in the Asian Games by winning a medal for the country,” he said.Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Tinku Roy, Agartala Mayor Dipak Majumder and Arjuna award-winning gymnast Dipa Karmakar were among those who attended the felicitation ceremony.
Article Summary: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey. The state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house. The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth games gold medal.

Article Title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
Article Text:
Are sports bodies of Indian states promoting the game properly?

Medal tally of India's athletes by birth state/UT

Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off it

Manipur still talking about 2023

Rajasthan: 14 years and counting

Uttar Pradesh and Delhi carry the same gloomy picture

And then come Tamil Nadu and others

The ones somewhere in the middle

How active are states/UTs with CWG medallists in promoting sport

Does it matter so much?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Social media presence Local sports events Government funding 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.No state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Facebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.And yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. It’s the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.If there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Its X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Gulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.Delhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.Set against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.Not every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation Silence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.
Article Summary: India won 39 medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Haryana produced 11 medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze. But the state sports department has posted just once in all of 2026. What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Government funding or social media presence? Share your view.

Article Title: ‘That video was not ordinary’: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi shares a light moment with boxer Lovlina Borgohain. (PTI Photo)

‘That video was not ordinary’

Mirabai opens up about four difficult years

Narender's joke leaves Modi laughing
